query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Buckets crew service into meaningful qualitative tiers (exceptional/professional/indifferent/rude), a useful grouping axis for a 'key points' review analysis, though it partly overlaps the existing numeric Staff Service rating. Groundedness is mixed: welcoming/caring-crew rows map correctly (samples 1,4,5) and a hospitality mention maps to professional_standard (sample 3), but sample 2 — a review purely about dreadful seats that says nothing about the crew — is labelled 'indifferent_minimal'. With only 11 NULLs, silent rows are being forced into a category, i.e. inferred negatives not supported by text.

per_column.name: operational_reliability
per_column.rationale: Delay/cancellation status is a genuinely new analytical axis absent from the original columns and valuable for spotting operational pain points. However groundedness is weak: 'on_time_smooth' is assigned to 5619 rows and, in every provided sample (1–5), none of the reviews mention timing at all yet all are stamped 'on_time_smooth'. Treating silence as a confident on-time assertion is an invented fact; the correct behaviour would be NULL/unknown for those rows.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_configuration
per_column.rationale: Adds a qualitative seat descriptor (spacious/adequate/narrow/hard-broken) that complements the numeric Seat Comfort rating; useful though partially redundant. Groundedness is strong: it leaves 3494 rows NULL, correctly abstains on silent rows (sample 3 → Unknown), and the labelled samples are sound readings — narrow/poor-padding → narrow_cramped (2), spacious/comfortable → spacious_comfortable (1,4,5).

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: In principle a distinct axis (query/complaint handling) but it risks conflation with onboard crew and only partially adds leverage beyond cabin_crew_service_quality. Groundedness is uneven: samples 2–4 correctly return Unknown, but with just 255 NULLs across the table the category is over-applied, and samples 1/5 derive 'responsive_proactive' from friendly onboard crew rather than any actual customer-service interaction — an unwarranted extrapolation.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Check-in/boarding/baggage handling is a legitimate new axis for the analysis. But groundedness is poor: only 300 NULLs, and all four applicable samples (1–4) discuss purely inflight experience yet are assigned ground-service verdicts (efficient_courteous_smooth / standard_transactional). These values are fabricated from text that is silent on ground handling.

judge.rationale: As a set the added columns open several new axes relevant to 'what should I concentrate on' — operational reliability, ground service, seat configuration and two service-quality lenses — going beyond the original numeric ratings and giving real grouping/comparison leverage (there is some overlap with existing Staff Service / Seat Comfort ratings and between the two service columns, but each still adds an angle). The main weakness is source groundedness: operational_reliability and ground_service_quality (and to a lesser degree cabin_crew and customer_service) assert confident categories on rows whose text is silent, evidenced by tiny NULL counts and samples where inflight-only reviews are stamped 'on_time_smooth' and given ground-service verdicts. seat_comfort_configuration is the model behaviour — it abstains with NULL when the text is silent. Overall usefulness is solid; groundedness is dragged down by systematic default-value hallucination on unmentioned aspects.
